issue.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/encode/starlette/discussions/2111
Originally posted by **falkoschindler** April 4, 2023 It looks like there is something wrong in `StaticFiles.loopup_path`. On venvs on Windows we noticed a problem with the common prefix check. Consider the following test script (here I'm refering to our library called NiceGUI, but any other side package should give a similar result): ```py from nicegui import ui directory = Path(ui.__file__).parent / 'static' print(f'{directory = }') print(f'{os.path.abspath(directory) = }') print(f'{os.path.realpath(directory) = }') ``` This yields the following output: ``` directory = WindowsPath('C:/Users/username/Envs/venv_name/lib/site-packages/nicegui/static') os.path.abspath(directory) = 'C:\\Users\\username\\Envs\\venv_name\\lib\\site-packages\\nicegui\\static' os.path.realpath(directory) = 'C:\\Users\\username\\Envs\\venv_name\\Lib\\site-packages\\nicegui\\static' ``` Note that `realpath` returns an uppercase "Lib" while `abspath` doesn't. This causes the common prefix to be only "C:\Users\username\Envs\venv_name\", which is outside of the `directory`. Therefore the following check is true and the directory is not served: https://github.com/encode/starlette/blob/f7bf74194358cceb5708f758989df89240c0c1aa/starlette/staticfiles.py#L172 I'm not perfectly sure how to fix it. Maybe using `commonpath` instead of `commonprefix`? Maybe converting strings to lowercase first? Maybe using pathlib instead of os.path? Anyway, it's an issue which confused us quite a bit over here: https://github.com/zauberzeug/nicegui/issues/714
issue.title: StaticFiles with follow_symlink not working correctly in venvs on Windows.
